root_cause.text: The NetLabel unlabeled address and mask attributes in the Generic Netlink policy were defined with NLA_BINARY (maximum length) rather than exact length, allowing a crafted request to supply a mask attribute shorter than the expected `struct in_addr`/`struct in6_addr`, while `netlbl_unlabel_addrinfo_get()` only checked the address length and compared mask length to that address length without independently validating the mask attribute's actual length, leading to an out-of-bounds read when the short mask is later treated as a full structure.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states "did not independently validate the corresponding mask attribute length" and "NLA_BINARY policy lengths are maximum lengths by default, so use NLA_POLICY_EXACT_LEN()". The patch changes the policy entries from `NLA_BINARY` with `.len` to `NLA_POLICY_EXACT_LEN()` and removes the `nla_len` checks in `netlbl_unlabel_addrinfo_get()`, confirming the flaw.
